prerequisites: Requirements for admission to the Master's program.

Degrees and master's degrees whose curricula ensure the acquisition of basic and common training competencies for the telecommunication branch (order CIN/352/2009), and which do not provide specific technology competencies related to automation.

Degrees and master's degrees whose plans conform, regarding basic and common training competencies for the computer science branch, to the resolution of June 8, 2009, of the General Secretariat of Universities, which publicizes the Agreement of the Council of Universities, establishing recommendations for the proposal by universities of official degree applications in the fields of Computer Engineering, Technical Computer Engineering, and Chemical Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context

That students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study

That students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments
That students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously
That students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous
Draft, scientifically interpret and orally communicate, to specialized audiences, documents within the scope of the master's lines.

Specify, design, develop, install, commission and maintain the hardware and software computer architecture of an industrial plant, including automation systems based on programmable controllers and industrial inspection systems for quality control, predictive maintenance and process knowledge improvement.
Use the acquired knowledge to maintain a critical and active attitude in the management of automation projects.
Compare and evaluate commercial systems and technologies for process automation, selecting the most appropriate for a given application.
Design efficient automated systems using the most appropriate architecture for each case.
Understand the general structure of process automation and supervision systems, identifying their fundamental parts, technological components of each of them, and their relationships.
Understand the circuits and discrete elements of implementation technologies for the control part based on wired logic, acquiring the ability to analyze and basic design of these.
Interpret professional diagrams of automation systems using multiple technologies: pneumatic, hydraulic, electrical, digital regulators, and PLCs.
Program simple control and supervision applications for processes based on PLCs and HMI-SCADA interfaces. Commissioning of systems.

syllabus_topics: Theme 1: INTRODUCTION. Structure of the automated system, components and their functional relationships. Architecture of the productive system organization.
Theme 2: FUNDAMENTALS OF AUTOMATION. Wired Logic. Electrical Technology. Pneumatic Technology. Programmed Logic. Microcontrollers. PLCs. PCs. Digital regulators.
Theme 3: PROCESS SUPERVISION. Control, Supervision and monitoring. HMIs and SCADAS.
Theme 4. MODELING OF DISCRETE EVENT PROCESSES. GRAFCET.
assessment_rules: A minimum score of 5 out of 10 points must be achieved in each assessment component to pass the course. The final grade will be calculated as: Final Grade = (EXT * P_EXT) + (TP * P_TP) + (EXP * P_EXP), where P_EXT is maximum 80%, P_TP is minimum 20%, and P_EXP is minimum 20%. Scores obtained in each test can be maintained across different calls of the same academic year. In case of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, a face-to-face defense may be requested.
